newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria sentences 22 people to death for graft.
newsitem.headline: Algeria sentences 22 people to death for graft.

text.p: An Algerian court sentenced 22 people to death in absentia for embezzling assets of a state-owned enterprise, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Sunday.
The court in Djelfa, 230 km (140 miles) south of Algiers, condemned the 22 people on Saturday at a hearing attended by 25 lawyers, APS said.
They were convicted for "misappropriating state funds and their use for personal benefits", it added.
Another 46 people are being tried by the same tribunal on charges of embezzling from the same company, a state-owned food distributor, APS said.
It was not clear how many were actually in detention.

The death sentence passed on the 22 was the harshest penalty imposed since Algerian authorities began issuing a stream of charges and jail sentences on senior officials in state-run firms in a crackdown on graft which started early in 1996.
Algerian President Liamine Zeroual vowed to Algerians in a presidential campaign late in 1995 that he would try to wipe out corruption.
Local politicians and ordinary Algerians blame corruption as a main factor in distrust between the nation's 29 million people and the authorities.
